why: Must_not 1 is avoided. Check 3 compares every exported function against the README headings, and its FAIL condition says "check it [slugify] specifically", so a README with only a padLeft section can't pass. Checks 1, 2 and 4 don't require a parameter count or a one-character fill, and the layout points are marked "Advisory (not PASS/FAIL conditions)". Must_not 2 breaks at Check 3. Its PASS condition requires the command to print "missing:" with nothing after it. The command sits inside a double-quoted bash string, and bash turns `'\\b'` into `'\b'`, which JavaScript reads as a backspace character. The regex is then backspace+name+backspace, which never matches a real heading. Every function is reported missing, so the check fails even on a correct pull request. That makes the PASS condition stricter than line 3, which only asks for a section per exported function.
